content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese with fruit is a soft, low‑fat (usually 1–2 %) curd cheese that contains pieces of fresh or dried fruit. It has a mild creamy taste, a slight tang, and sweet fruit notes, making it a popular breakfast or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy products, known already in ancient Egypt.
Low‑fat versions are widely used in diet plans because they are low in calories but high in protein.
Adding fruit boosts the content of vitamins C and A as well as antioxidants.
Cottage cheese is easily digested and often recommended for children and convalescents.
The product is called cottage cheese in the US and творог in Russia.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese provides about 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Fat usually does not exceed 2 %, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: It is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamins B2 and B12, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fruit benefits
items.content: Fruit adds dietary fiber, vitamins C and A, and natural antioxidants.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cottage cheese contains lactose, so people with intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein, the main milk protein.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared versions can contain added salt; those monitoring sodium should check the label.

items.title: Sugar in fruit
items.content: Dried fruits can raise blood sugar levels; diabetics should prefer fresh fruit without added sugar.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy cottage cheese with fruit as a snack, blend it into smoothies, use it as a filling for pancakes or casseroles, or layer it in dessert parfaits. It also pairs well with honey, nuts, or whole‑grain cereals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. Fresh product remains good for 5–7 days. Freezing may affect texture, so freeze only for long‑term storage.
